account:
Today is day 1, just after ten. I have come to the mill for my scheduled grain inspection, but have not yet identified anyone overseeing it or inspected the grain. Several townsfolk are clustered near the mill and bakery. They keep repeating a vague report about a bridge or port change at the bakery. Townsfolk 11 named the baker and freight as people who were there, but gave no actual proposal, details, or firsthand explanation. Yesterday the neighbour also mentioned a vague report near the bakery. This repetition is unusual, but it does not establish that any public change has been proposed or approved. I do not yet know what the reported change is for.

The secretary checked the office records and found no bridge or port proposal, council correspondence, or accounts ledger. The treasury held only 128 emeralds. Neither neighbour nor freight supplied firsthand proposal evidence to the secretary. I have authorized enquiries among town hall staff about where accounts and council letters are deposited, with a report at thirteen hundred. These missing records remain unresolved, not proof of wrongdoing.

A community gathering with the innkeeper is confirmed for eighteen hundred in the great hall. I approved it yesterday, and today approved freight escorting me there from the office. The innkeeper wanted to discuss catering privately with the secretary; that is consistent with preparations for the gathering, though I did not hear their private discussion. I have no evidence connecting the gathering or escort to the bridge rumour. My remaining appointments include lunch at home at twelve, council letters at thirteen, tea with the neighbour at the east dockside cottage at fifteen, and office business at sixteen-thirty.
